title: Second Largest Distinct Value
statement:
Find the second-largest **distinct** value -- the largest value that is strictly smaller than the maximum -- and say so honestly when there is none.

## Your function

```
std::optional<int> SecondLargest(const std::vector<int>& values);
```

Return the second-largest distinct value, or `std::nullopt` if the vector has fewer than two distinct values (empty, one element, or all equal).

```
[5 9 2 9]   ->  5      (the two 9s are one value)
[4 4 4]     ->  none
```

## Watch out

- **Duplicates of the maximum are not the second largest.** `[9, 9, 5]` has second-largest `5`, not `9`.
- **Do not use a sentinel like `INT_MIN` for "nothing yet".** An array containing `INT_MIN` is legitimate, and a sentinel cannot tell it apart from "unset". `std::optional` exists for exactly this.
- A single pass with two running values avoids sorting; sorting and de-duplicating is also fine.

tests.name: duplicates of the maximum
tests.description: The two 9s are one value; the answer is 5.

tests.name: INT_MIN is a real value
tests.description: A sentinel of INT_MIN would wrongly report none.
